meta.label: Headphones and earbuds
tradeoffLabels: easiest to repair or replace parts
meta.attribution: Repairability scores for wireless models come from iFixit's published wireless earbud and wireless headphone repairability tables, which score a teardown from zero (hardest to repair) to ten (easiest), converted here to a 0-100 scale; for a model not yet in a table, the score comes from iFixit's own teardown of it. Wired models have no such table; their repairability score instead reflects the maker's own published spare parts and cable listings, a different kind of evidence, noted where it applies. Battery life, price and warranty figures come from each maker's own product or support page on the date shown; where a maker's site could not be reached or did not state a figure, that cell is left blank rather than guessed. Privacy notes summarize what each maker's own privacy policy says it collects through the product and its companion app; a shorter note reflects a shorter policy passage, not less data collected. Several entries note the EU's USB-C charging rule for headsets and earbuds, Directive 2022/2380, where it applies to that model. Sound quality is not scored: it is a matter of taste this catalogue has no independent way to test, unlike whether a battery can be replaced. Reviewed 2026-08; nine models added and checked 2026-10. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare headphones and earbuds by repairability, support life, cost, and privacy.

axes.question: Lower cost or a stronger overall fit?

criteria.label: Battery life and whether it can be replaced
Data the device or app collects

products.name: Fairphone Fairbuds XL
products.description: Fairphone's over-ear noise-cancelling headphones, built around nine replaceable parts including a battery the owner can swap out with a screwdriver.

repairability.note: iFixit's wireless headphones repairability table gives the Fairbuds XL a perfect 10 out of 10, the highest score in the table, matched only by its own 2023 version, for a design with no glue that can be opened with ordinary screws.

longevity.note: Fairphone's own product page lists up to 30 hours of playback with noise cancelling off, or 26 hours with it on, and says the battery can be swapped out by the owner; coverage is a 2-year warranty extendable to 3 years.

accessibility.note: Fairbuds XL charge over USB-C. EU Directive 2022/2380 has required USB-C charging on headsets sold in the EU since 28 December 2024, and Fairphone's primary retail market is the EU.

products.name: Fairphone Fairbuds
products.description: Fairphone's true wireless earbuds, with batteries in both the earbuds and the charging case that the owner can replace.

repairability.note: iFixit's wireless earbud repairability table, and the downloadable score list it links to, score the Fairbuds 10 out of 10, the highest of any earbud in the table, citing coin-cell earbud batteries that are very easy to replace, a highly modular charging case, and Fairphone's commitment to official replacement parts and instructions.

longevity.note: Fairphone's own product page says each earbud runs a 45mAh battery for up to 6 hours, with the 500mAh charging case adding another 20 hours for 26 hours total, and that the batteries in both the earbuds and the case can be replaced; coverage is a 2-year warranty, extendable to 3 years by registering online.

economical.note: Fairphone's own site prices the Fairbuds at 99 euros.

accessibility.note: Fairphone sells the Fairbuds directly online with a 14-day trial period and lists physical retail locations through a store locator, concentrated in Europe.

products.name: Sennheiser HD 600
products.description: A wired, open-back reference headphone with a detachable cable and a spare-parts store, popular with people who mix and master audio.

repairability.note: Sennheiser's own store sells replacement earpads for the HD 600 at $54.95 and describes a detachable cable with a 6.3mm connector and a bundled 3.5mm adapter, so the two parts most likely to wear out can be bought and swapped.

longevity.note: The HD 600 is a fully wired, passive design with no battery to wear out. Sennheiser's own listing includes a 2-year manufacturer warranty.

economical.note: Sennheiser's own store prices the HD 600 at $499.95, including the 2-year warranty and expedited shipping.

privacy.note: Sennheiser's own listing describes only a wired analogue connection, with no Bluetooth radio, companion app or account for the HD 600, so there is no described channel for it to collect usage data.

accessibility.note: Sold directly through Sennheiser's own online store rather than mainstream electronics retail; using it well also requires an amplifier or a source device with enough power to drive it.

products.name: Shure SE215
products.description: A wired in-ear monitor built for musicians, with a detachable MMCX cable that Shure sells as a separate replacement part.

repairability.note: Shure's own SE215 listing describes a detachable 3.5mm cable with an MMCX connector, and Shure sells official replacement cables (EAC64, EAC46) plus several ear-sleeve materials and sizes as separate accessories.

longevity.note: The SE215 is a passive wired earphone with no battery. Shure's own listing states the box includes a 2-year warranty.

privacy.note: Shure's own listing for the standard SE215 describes a cable and ear sleeves only, with no Bluetooth, app or account mentioned.

products.name: Apple AirPods Pro 3
products.description: Apple's current noise-cancelling earbuds and the most widely used premium earbud in this roster, with a sealed, glued battery.

repairability.note: iFixit's teardown gave the AirPods Pro 3 a 0 out of 10 repairability score, writing that the coin-cell battery is glued down so firmly that only heat, tweezers and luck will free it, and that flex cables run through solder points and glued channels that make reassembly nearly impossible.

longevity.note: Apple's own product page lists up to 8 hours of listening time per charge with Active Noise Cancellation on, extending to 10 hours with the Hearing Aid feature active in Transparency mode, about 4 hours more than the previous generation.

economical.note: Apple's own store prices the AirPods Pro 3 at $249.

privacy.note: Apple's privacy policy says it collects precise location 'to support services such as Find My,' plus usage data including app launches, product interaction and diagnostic data; it has no separate section for hearing or listening data.

accessibility.note: AirPods Pro 3 charge from a USB-C case. EU Directive 2022/2380 has required USB-C charging on earbuds sold in the EU since 28 December 2024, a standard Apple's case-based AirPods line already met.

products.name: Apple AirPods Max 2
products.description: Apple's over-ear noise-cancelling headphones, scoring the same modest repairability as the original 2020 model.

repairability.note: iFixit's wireless headphones table scores the AirPods Max 2 4 out of 10, the same score it gives the original 2020 AirPods Max.

longevity.note: Apple's own page lists up to 20 hours of listening or movie watching with Active Noise Cancellation and Spatial Audio on, and the headphones charge over USB-C, the same cable used by iPhone, iPad and Mac.

economical.note: Apple's own store prices the AirPods Max 2 at $549 across all five colors, with no difference in price between them.

privacy.note: Apple's privacy policy lists 'Health Information' and 'Fitness Information' as categories collected only when a user chooses to share them, alongside general app usage and diagnostic data; it has no section specific to headphone audio data.

accessibility.note: AirPods Max 2 charge over USB-C. EU Directive 2022/2380 has required USB-C charging on headsets sold in the EU since 28 December 2024, a requirement this model meets.

products.name: Samsung Galaxy Buds Pro
products.description: Samsung's earbuds, with a charging case that is easy to open but a driver iFixit calls practically inaccessible.

repairability.note: iFixit's teardown scored the Galaxy Buds Pro 3 out of 10: the charging case battery is modular and easy to replace, but the earbuds' own batteries use soldered connections and the drivers are practically inaccessible, making replacement tedious at best and more likely destructive.

privacy.note: Samsung's privacy policy states it collects recordings of a user's voice when voice commands are enabled and used, plus device identifiers and usage and log information; it says biometric data used for on-device features is not transferred to Samsung.

products.name: Sony WH-1000XM6
products.description: Sony's current flagship noise-cancelling headphones, redesigned to secure the battery with screws instead of adhesive.

repairability.note: iFixit's teardown found the WH-1000XM6 battery 'housed and secured with two screws' rather than glued as in the previous XM5, calling it simple, effective and reusable, with a modular USB-C port, audio jack and button board; iFixit's wireless headphones table rates the result 6 out of 10, and Sony had already published a right-to-repair manual for the prior XM5.

accessibility.note: The WH-1000XM6 is a headset with a rechargeable battery, which puts it within EU Directive 2022/2380's USB-C charging requirement for headsets sold in the EU, in force since 28 December 2024, on top of the screw-secured battery iFixit found inside it.

products.name: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones
products.description: Bose's flagship noise-cancelling headphones, with an optional paid plan that extends battery-failure coverage past the first year.

longevity.note: Bose's own product page lists up to 30 hours of battery life (23 hours with Immersive Audio on), backed by a 1-year limited warranty covering mechanical breakdown and battery failure; a $59.95 BoseCare Protection Plan extends battery-failure coverage through years two and three.

economical.note: Bose's own store prices the QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) at $449.

privacy.note: Bose's privacy policy lists collecting sensor data such as head orientation and movement and wearable fit information, plus 'noise levels and audio frequencies of sounds around you,' as data gathered through its products and apps.

accessibility.note: The QuietComfort Ultra Headphones charge over USB-C, which Bose's own page confirms; that charging port is not optional in the EU, where Directive 2022/2380 has required USB-C on headsets since 28 December 2024.

products.name: Beats Studio Pro
products.description: Apple-owned Beats' over-ear noise-cancelling headphones, scored among the least repairable in iFixit's table.

repairability.note: iFixit's wireless headphones repairability table scores the Beats Studio Pro 2 out of 10, the same score it gives the Beats Solo 4, among the lowest results in the table.

longevity.note: Beats' own product page lists up to 40 hours of listening time with Active Noise Cancellation off, or 24 hours with ANC or Transparency mode on, plus a Fast Fuel feature giving about 4 hours of playback from a 10-minute charge when the battery is low.

economical.note: Beats' own site lists the Studio Pro at $349.99.

privacy.note: Beats routes warranty service through Apple, and Beats products fall under Apple's privacy policy, which says Apple aims to collect only the personal data it needs and directs users to product-specific privacy details shown at the point of use rather than a headphone-specific list on the general policy page.

accessibility.note: Beats' own page lists USB-C charging for the Studio Pro, which EU Directive 2022/2380 has made mandatory for headsets sold in the EU since 28 December 2024.

products.name: JBL Tune 520BT
products.description: A budget on-ear Bluetooth headphone from JBL, one of the most widely stocked headphone brands.

repairability.note: iFixit's wireless headphones repairability table scores the JBL Tune 520BT 4 out of 10.

accessibility.note: EU Directive 2022/2380 requires headsets with a rechargeable battery sold in the EU to charge over USB-C, a rule in force since 28 December 2024 that covers the Tune 520BT.

products.name: Anker Soundcore Q20i
products.description: A budget noise-cancelling headphone from Anker's Soundcore line, with a long stated battery life but a low repairability score.

repairability.note: iFixit's wireless headphones repairability table scores the Soundcore Q20i 2 out of 10, in the same low band as the Beats models it tested.

longevity.note: Soundcore's own EU product page lists 60 hours of playback with Active Noise Cancellation off, or 40 hours with it on, and says a 5-minute charge adds about 4 hours of playtime.

economical.note: Soundcore's EU store price on the date checked was 52.99 euros, marked down from 69.99 euros.

privacy.note: Soundcore's privacy notice for its speaker and headphone products says it collects entertainment preferences such as audio settings, and with permission accesses call status and the microphone for speech features.

accessibility.note: The Q20i is sold widely direct-to-consumer and through Amazon; in the EU specifically, Directive 2022/2380 has required its USB-C charging port on headsets since 28 December 2024.

products.name: Skullcandy Crusher ANC 2
products.description: A bass-forward budget over-ear headphone from Skullcandy, scored among the least repairable in iFixit's table.

repairability.note: iFixit's wireless headphones repairability table scores the Skullcandy Crusher ANC 2 2 out of 10.

products.name: Google Pixel Buds Pro 2
products.description: Google's noise-cancelling earbuds, paired with Google's account-wide data collection.

longevity.note: Google's own Pixel Buds specification page lists up to 8 hours of listening time with Active Noise Cancellation on, or 30 hours including the charging case, and an IP54 rating for the earbuds.

privacy.note: Google's privacy policy says that for voice-activated features, Google records a user's voice and audio plus a few seconds before activation, alongside device identifiers and sensor data such as accelerometer and gyroscope readings.

accessibility.note: Pixel Buds Pro 2 charge over USB-C with optional Qi wireless charging. EU Directive 2022/2380 has required USB-C charging on earbuds sold in the EU since 28 December 2024, a standard this model already met.

products.name: Apple EarPods (USB-C)
products.description: Apple's basic wired earbuds, with a USB-C plug and no battery of their own to wear out.

longevity.note: Target's listing describes these as wired earbuds with a USB-C connector and a built-in remote for volume, playback and calls; being wired, there is no battery inside the earbuds themselves to degrade.

economical.note: Target's listing prices the Apple EarPods (USB-C) at $19.99, the cheapest item in this roster.

privacy.note: Target's listing describes only a wired USB-C connector and an inline remote, with no Bluetooth radio, companion app or account for the standard wired EarPods.

accessibility.note: Sold at Target and Apple's own store alongside other iPhone accessories; there is no pairing, charging or app setup needed before first use.

products.name: Apple AirPods 5
products.description: Apple's 2026 entry-level noise-cancelling earbuds, and the first AirPods iFixit has scored above zero for repairability.

repairability.note: iFixit's AirPods 5 teardown scores them 2 out of 10, the first AirPods to score above 0: each earbud battery now plugs in on prongs that iFixit calls 'intuitive to unplug', but the left and right batteries are not interchangeable, replacement cells were not yet on sale, the charging case was destroyed reaching its battery, and Apple offers no replacement parts or repair manuals.

longevity.note: Apple's own product page lists up to 4 hours of listening per charge with Active Noise Cancellation (5 hours with the Wireless Charging Case) and up to 22 hours in total with the wireless case. Apple's AirPods service page says that under AppleCare it replaces the battery at no extra charge once capacity drops below 80%; without it, the battery iFixit found is not sold as a part.

economical.note: Apple's own store prices the AirPods 5 at $129, or $149 with the Wireless Charging Case.

privacy.note: Apple's privacy policy says it collects precise location 'only to support services such as Find My' or where the user agrees, plus usage data including product interaction and diagnostic data; Apple's AirPods 5 page highlights Find My tracking for the earbuds. The policy has no section specific to earbud audio data.

accessibility.note: Sold through Apple's own online store in two versions, with and without a wireless charging case, both charging over USB-C; Apple notes that no charge cable or power adapter is included in the box.

products.name: Google Pixel Buds 2a
products.description: Google's lower-priced noise-cancelling earbuds, with a charging case built for repair and earbuds that are not.

repairability.note: iFixit's teardown gives the Pixel Buds 2a a 'provisional repairability score of 4 out of 10': the charging case battery pops out in a tray with a pull tab, but the earbud battery is glued in so tightly that removing it destroyed both the casing and the battery, even though Google's repair manual site publishes a battery replacement guide for them.

longevity.note: Google's own store page lists up to 7 hours of listening with Active Noise Cancellation on and 20 hours in total with the charging case (10 and 27 hours with it off); iFixit's earbud table says that once the earbud batteries degrade, they are e-waste.

economical.note: Google's own store prices the Pixel Buds 2a at $129.

privacy.note: Google's privacy policy says that when a device detects an audio activation command, Google records the user's voice and audio plus a few seconds before activation, and that device sensors such as an accelerometer can be used to understand location and movement.

accessibility.note: Sold directly through the Google Store; Google's page says they pair with an Android phone using Fast Pair, so setup is quickest for Android users.

products.name: Sony WH-CH720N
products.description: Sony's lower-priced noise-cancelling headphones, with a battery iFixit found straightforward to replace.

repairability.note: iFixit's wireless headphones repairability table scores the WH-CH720N 4 out of 10: the battery uses a standard connector and only mild adhesive, making replacement straightforward, but the USB-C port and driver wires are soldered to the board, and Sony does not provide repair manuals or spare parts.

longevity.note: Sony's own product page lists up to 35 hours of music playback (with DSEE off and the AAC codec) and supports quick charging; the battery itself is one iFixit rates straightforward to swap.

economical.note: Sony's own US store lists the WH-CH720N at an MSRP of $179.99, noting it goes on sale from time to time.

privacy.note: The privacy policy for Sony's Sound Connect headphone app lists device and advertising IDs, how the user uses the headphones and app, and optional listening history; it says Sony may build profiles and, with consent, share data with its local Sony company for targeted advertising, while location-based features run on the phone and 'SONY will not collect location data or track your location'.

accessibility.note: Sold through Sony's own US store, which offers group discounts for education, healthcare and military buyers and a loyalty points programme; ambient sound settings are adjusted through the Sony Sound Connect app.

products.name: Beats Solo 4
products.description: Apple-owned Beats' on-ear wireless headphones, with long battery life but a glued-in battery.

repairability.note: iFixit's wireless headphones repairability table scores the Beats Solo 4 2 out of 10: the ear cushions are glued on, the battery is firmly glued in place, hot glue and soldered connections hamper port and driver repairs, and Apple does not support Beats headphones with repair manuals or spare parts.

longevity.note: Beats' own product page lists up to 50 hours of listening on a single charge, with a 10-minute Fast Fuel charge giving up to 5 hours, and USB-C charging; the battery inside is one iFixit found firmly glued.

economical.note: Beats' own site lists the Solo 4 at $199.99.

privacy.note: Beats products fall under Apple's privacy policy, which lists usage data such as product interaction and diagnostic data, and precise location only to support services such as Find My or where the user agrees; it has no headphone-specific section.

accessibility.note: Sold through Beats' own site, and works over Bluetooth or a wired USB-C or 3.5 mm cable, so it stays usable with devices that lack Bluetooth.

products.name: Sennheiser Momentum 4 Wireless
products.description: Sennheiser's noise-cancelling headphones, known for a 60-hour battery, with snap-in ear cushions but a glued battery.

repairability.note: iFixit's wireless headphones repairability table scores the Momentum 4 5 out of 10: the snap-in ear cushions need no tools and the headband cushion and charge port can be replaced with basic tools, but the battery is firmly glued and the driver connections are soldered; apart from ear cushions, Sennheiser provides no repair parts or instructions.

longevity.note: Sennheiser's own US store lists up to 60 hours of playback with ANC on, plus 6 hours from a 10-minute charge, and includes a 1-year manufacturer warranty, with paid extended warranty coverage offered.

economical.note: Sennheiser's own US store lists the Momentum 4 Wireless at $299.95, shown on the date checked at a sale price of $229.95.

privacy.note: Sennheiser's Smart Control Plus app privacy notice says the app collects product analytics such as operating time, ANC use, charging cycles and playback counts, plus Google Analytics and Firebase data; location access needed on Android is not transferred to Sennheiser, and an account (which syncs EQ settings and a sound personalisation profile) is optional.

accessibility.note: Sold through Sennheiser's own US store, operated by Sonova Consumer Hearing USA, with free expedited shipping; sound settings run through the Smart Control app.

products.name: Marshall Monitor III A.N.C.
products.description: Marshall's noise-cancelling over-ear headphones, sold with user-replaceable spare parts and a very long stated battery life.

repairability.note: iFixit's wireless headphones repairability table scores the Monitor III 5 out of 10: twist-off ear cushions, a screwed-on headband cushion and clearly marked battery compartments make for straightforward repairs and both batteries use standard connectors, but the USB-C port and ANC mic wires are soldered. Marshall's own page says the model has user-replaceable spare parts, sold through marshall.com.

longevity.note: Marshall's own product page lists 70 hours of playtime with ANC and 100 hours without, 12 hours from a 15-minute charge, a battery preservation mode, and user-replaceable spare parts with authorised repair available through marshall.com; it states a minimum of 2 years of software and firmware updates from when the product was last sold.

economical.note: Marshall's own US store lists the Monitor III A.N.C. at $379.99 in its product data.

privacy.note: Marshall's privacy notice covers its websites and app; for app use it lists only an email address, processed on consent when users sign up, while website visitors who consent are tracked with Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity and advertising pixels from Google, Meta and TikTok.

accessibility.note: Sold through Marshall's own store, which advertises 25% off for students; it ships with a USB-C to 3.5 mm cord so it can also be used wired, and spare parts are available through marshall.com.

products.name: Audio-Technica ATH-M50x
products.description: A long-selling wired studio headphone with detachable cables and maker-sold replacement earpads and headband.

repairability.note: Audio-Technica's own ATH-M50x page lists 3 detachable cables and sells an HP-HBM50x replacement headband for $17.00; its HP-EP M-Series replacement earpads are listed as compatible with the ATH-M50x. iFixit's ATH-M50x device page hosts a community teardown.

longevity.note: The ATH-M50x is a passive wired headphone with no battery to wear out, and its cables, earpads and headband are sold as replacement parts by Audio-Technica.

economical.note: Audio-Technica's own US store prices the ATH-M50x at $159.00.

privacy.note: Audio-Technica's listing describes a wired, closed-back headphone with detachable cables and no Bluetooth radio, app or account, so there is no described channel for it to collect usage data.

accessibility.note: Sold through Audio-Technica's own US store with free 2-day shipping and through a network of authorised resellers; it plugs into any device with a headphone jack or adapter, with no pairing or charging.

products.name: Beyerdynamic DT 770 PRO
products.description: A closed-back wired studio headphone made since 1985 and handcrafted in Germany, built so its parts can be replaced.

repairability.note: Beyerdynamic's own page says the DT 770 PRO is handcrafted in Germany and that 'all the components used are replaceable if necessary', with replaceable ear pads, though the classic model has a fixed rather than detachable cable. Beyerdynamic's spare-parts store lists ear pad sets for the DT 770 PRO, and iFixit's device page confirms user-replaceable earpads and headband.

longevity.note: The DT 770 PRO is a passive wired headphone with no battery; Beyerdynamic's page lists up to 2 years of warranty and says the models are designed for long-term use thanks to replaceable components. iFixit dates the model's first release to 1985.

economical.note: Beyerdynamic's own North American store prices the DT 770 PRO at $199.99.

privacy.note: Beyerdynamic's listing describes a straight cable with a 3.5 mm plug and 6.35 mm adapter, with no Bluetooth radio, app or account, so there is no described channel for it to collect usage data.

accessibility.note: Offered in 32, 80 and 250 ohm versions; the higher-impedance versions are built for studio equipment and may need an amplifier, so buyers have to pick the right version for a phone or laptop.

products.name: Koss Porta Pro
products.description: A cheap folding wired headphone sold since 1984, covered by a limited lifetime warranty.

repairability.note: Koss sells Porta Pro ear cushions for $5.00 a set (two pairs of ear cushions and two pairs of temple pads), but the cable is fixed rather than detachable, so a broken cord means warranty service or soldering; iFixit's Porta Pro device page lists a speaker-holder replacement guide.

longevity.note: The Porta Pro is a passive wired headphone with no battery. Koss's product page says all Koss wired headphones are covered by a 'Limited Lifetime Warranty', and its warranty page says US owners send the product in with $9.00 return shipping and handling to have it repaired or replaced.

economical.note: Koss's own store prices the Porta Pro at $49.99.

privacy.note: Koss's listing for the standard Porta Pro describes a 4 ft cord with a 3.5 mm plug and no Bluetooth radio, app or account, so there is no described channel for it to collect usage data.

accessibility.note: Sold through Koss's own store, which says international shipping is available to most countries and regions; it folds up to a compact size and needs no pairing or charging.

products.name: Repair the headphones you already own
products.description: The simplest route for most people: fixing a cable, an earpad or a battery instead of buying a replacement pair.

repairability.note: iFixit's headphone repair hub covers 51 brands and says the main wear points on headphones are cables and earpads; it stocks batteries, dozens of earpad varieties, cables, speakers and case parts, and recommends choosing headphones with replaceable cables and earpads for long-term value.

longevity.note: Fixing a fraying cable, worn earpad foam or a swappable battery keeps an existing pair working instead of buying a new one; iFixit's hub presents this as the more sustainable default before replacement.

accessibility.note: Repair requires finding the right guide and part for the exact model among iFixit's 51 covered brands, and often a tool such as a heat source or a spudger; it takes more effort than buying new but is usually cheaper than professional repair.

products.name: Back Market refurbished headphones
products.description: A marketplace for refurbished headphones and earbuds from major brands, best value when the exact model is chosen carefully.

repairability.note: Repairability after purchase depends entirely on the specific refurbished model chosen; iFixit's headphone repair hub covers 51 brands with widely varying parts and guide availability.

longevity.note: Back Market's site-wide 'Back Market Promise' advertises a 1-year warranty and free 30-day returns across the marketplace; the quality page's itemized inspection checklist names phones, tablets, smartwatches, laptops and game consoles specifically, and does not list headphones among those five categories.

accessibility.note: Back Market's headphones and earphones section lists refurbished units from Sony, Bose, Beats, Harman Kardon and other brands, alongside buying guides comparing Apple AirPods, Google Pixel Buds and Samsung earbuds.
